threads.body: [General] This deduplication also changes legacy telemetry. Lettuce 5 retries the same `ClusterCommand`/`AsyncCommand` after a MOVED response, so the previous advice started a span for each write; this unconditional guard now suppresses the retry span even when stable database semconv is disabled. That conflicts with the stated requirement that legacy telemetry remain unchanged. Gate the single-span behavior on `emitStableDatabaseSemconv()` while retaining last-peer replacement for stable spans, and make the legacy MOVED assertion cover the prior span count.

Addressed in 85872068af1601186c35c543a51c91401894bbf8.

Analysis: The span-start guard applied to both semconv modes. A MOVED retry reuses the same AsyncCommand, so the guard reduced legacy telemetry from two root spans to one. The stable span still needs the guard because its peer fields update through the retry and must describe the completing connection.

Upsides: Legacy mode keeps one span per write, while stable mode keeps one span with the completing peer. The MOVED test now checks the mode-specific trace count and span attributes.

Downsides: The test uses a small mode-dependent trace assertion list because legacy and stable modes emit different numbers of traces.

threads.body: [General] A pending reactive Mono now leaks its span when cancelled after native subscription. `onCommand()` starts the span, but this handler inherits the default no-op `onCancel()` and only ends from success/error callbacks; Lettuce cancellation transitions the subscription to completed without sending either terminal signal. Override `onCancel()` to end an expected-response span and share an atomic once guard with the terminal callbacks so cancellation/completion races cannot record twice.

replies.body:
Addressed in c87614b3b466a4607eec9f1c1e048bdc1d019846.

Analysis: Lettuce calls the handler's cancellation hook after `onCommand()` starts the span, but the Mono handler did not override that hook. Cancellation can race with a success or error callback, so all expected-response completion paths must claim a shared once guard before ending the span.

Upsides: Pending Mono spans now end on cancellation, and terminal signal races cannot end a span twice. The isolated BLPOP test verifies cancellation exports the expected span without blocking the shared test connection.

Downsides: Each Mono subscription allocates one AtomicBoolean.

threads.body: `LettuceReactiveCommandSubscriber` intentionally swallows exceptions thrown by `handler.onCancel()` (it drops them via `Operators.onErrorDropped`), so `Subscription#cancel()` should not throw. This assertion will fail; update the test to assert cancellation does not throw and still cancels upstream (and optionally verify error-dropping via a Reactor hook if you want to validate the failure path).

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: Reactor 3.1 does not always swallow errors passed to Operators.onErrorDropped. With no local or global drop hook, Operators.onErrorDropped bubbles the error. That is the test's configuration, and the targeted test confirms the IllegalStateException remains the root cause while the finally block cancels upstream. Reactor 3.1 FluxPeek.cancel() also runs its doOnCancel callback before it cancels upstream and returns. The immediate cancelled assertion is therefore ordered by the dispose call, and the targeted integration test passed repeatedly.

Upsides: The tests keep checking the actual Reactor 3.1 contracts and will catch a regression in upstream cancellation or callback ordering.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: `commands` is stored by reference and later read to derive the peer address at span end. If the passed-in list is mutable (or reused by Lettuce), this can lead to incorrect peer attribution or `ConcurrentModificationException`. Prefer storing an immutable snapshot (e.g., `List.copyOf(commands)` or a defensive copy) when constructing `LettuceBatchRequest`.

replies.body:
Addressed in 85d23cc820f9d1d3364511311bb2ab9955d38e09.

Analysis: LettuceBatchRequest reads the command list again when the span ends, after the batch state has handed off its mutable buffer. Copying the list before deriving request fields keeps the request's command set stable while preserving later peer updates on each command object.

Upsides: Peer attribution cannot change because the source list is cleared or reused. All request fields now derive from the same snapshot. The regression test covers source-list mutation.

Downsides: Each batch request allocates one shallow ArrayList copy.

threads.body: If `onSpanEnding(...)` throws, `instrumenter().end(...)` will be skipped and the span may leak. Since this is agent code, it should be resilient to unexpected exceptions; wrap `onSpanEnding` in a `try/catch` (or `try/finally`) to ensure `instrumenter().end(...)` is always invoked.

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: LettuceFluxTerminationHandler is the only onSpanEnding override. It only reads the span from an OpenTelemetry context and sets two attributes. Those API calls have no expected exception path. A try/finally would address only a hypothetical future override and would still pass its exception into Reactor. A broad catch would instead hide an instrumentation defect. There is no current failure or unsafe input to guard.

Upsides: The terminal path stays direct and does not add a broad exception handler for OpenTelemetry API calls that are expected not to throw.

Downsides: A future onSpanEnding override that introduces a throwing operation would need its own error handling before it is safe to use here.
